decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate by a quarter point to 2.25 percent to continue pulling back on economic stimulus.

changes.quote: Output appears to be growing at a moderate pace despite the earlier rise in energy prices, and labor market conditions continue to improve gradually.
changes.explanation: The Fed believes the economy is strong enough to handle higher interest rates even with more expensive energy.

changes.quote: Inflation and longer-term inflation expectations remain well contained.
changes.explanation: Officials are not seeing signs that price increases are spiraling out of control.

changes.quote: In addition, the Committee unanimously decided to expedite the release of its minutes.
changes.explanation: The Fed is increasing transparency by releasing detailed meeting notes three weeks after each decision.

tone_quotes.quote: With underlying inflation expected to be relatively low, the Committee believes that policy accommodation can be removed at a pace that is likely to be measured.

The Committee believes that, even after this action, the stance of monetary policy remains accommodative and, coupled with robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing ongoing support to economic activity.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.02% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate; the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.81% would fall by about $3.82 a month if the -2 bp move in the 10-year Treasury passed through.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Employers added an average of 188k jobs a month over the prior 3 months while unemployment was 5.4%.

for_country.text: Core PCE inflation was 2.1%, which is slightly above the 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The Fed signals it will continue to raise interest rates at a measured pace in the coming months. It will adjust this plan if economic conditions or inflation risks change significantly.

citations.detail: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 2-1/4 percent.
